Underwhelming and disappointing
Sep 2026 • Solo
Pleasant ambience / it was very quiet for dinner tonight. Service is patchy, they try to please but language and communication really a bit hard going. 
“Could i have some peppermint tea please. Does it come in a pot?’

‘Uh, uh / pot?’

Yes, does your tea come in a pot and not just a cup?’

‘Let me check’

Or when the small solitary bread (and very pedestrian processed white) roll came, I said I try to avoid processed white bread. Could you let me have a grain or whole meal roll please? That provoked an exercise all in itself and she said ‘this is the only bread we serve’. I said for a restaurant purportedly of this caliber, surely there must be another tuition than a processed white flour roll..’. Hurried away, phone calls later, and she returned saying “we can let you have rye bread’. I said ok that’s fine thank you, only to have served 2 slices of brown bread instead. No grain rolls of any sort. 

I ordered the pork ribs. I had asked the previous day ( as an station at the Melia) when I was at the restaurant if it was a half or full rack of baby back ribs, and it prompted some quizzical stares and finger gesticulating to draw the imaginary size, which I surmised was a half rack. What came tonight however was 3 Ribs alongside a handful of potato wedges, which had clearly been cooked a while ago and was room temperature, no crispy surfaces - bordering on almost soggy. 

The accompanying corn on the cob was no better barely warm, and it could have been my imagination, but I took one bite and concluded it wasn’t fresh and had a slight stale taste. I left that. With how empty the restaurant was and without volume movement of its food, I dread to think what’s meant to be a fine dining restaurant can’t even get freshly cooked stapes to order, but is comfortable serving pre-cooked food. Microwaved probably. 

The half bulb of garlic was also room temperature, and hadn’t been roasted long enough to have the garlic segments mushy and sweet. It was almost crunchy / and when paired with it being lukewarm, and the garlic not having been cooked enough to caramelise and go mushy, was an unpleasant experience. I left that too. 

The ribs were .. ok. Not trimmed, fatty pieces galore, and was lukewarm when served.

All in, a very underwhelming experience, and not quite worth the dosh. The saving grace was - the views are spectacular, and the pot of tea was hot.
